headline: Conduit turns distributed RL experience handling into a runtime optimization surface
summary: Zhang et al. present Conduit, an Experience Data Plane that separates reinforcement-learning experience ingestion, placement and delivery from framework execution. The authors report up to 97% lower exposed experience-path latency and up to 38% lower end-to-end iteration latency in RLlib tests spanning DQN, SAC and PPO workloads on an eight-actor/eight-learner setup. They also report scaling from 8 to 1,024 AMD MI250X GPUs on a fixed workload, compared with Conduit without adaptive placement, and similar convergence curves in two tested tasks. These are author-reported results from one preprint, not an independent reproduction; transfer to other workloads and full cost/energy effects remain unmeasured.
